critique:
field green_cube_pos, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  DELETE. Every goal in this task names only the cubes whose containers must be lifted, and this field was carried through every episode without being read once: the green cube was never named, so its position never selected a target. Its fact is folded into target_cube_positions below, which records a position only for cubes the goal names, so a green cube is still recorded on any episode whose goal asks for it. Dropping it does not break NECESSITY because nothing in the subgoal rule ever consults it.

field blue_cube_pos, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  DELETE, folded into target_cube_positions. The per-color fields force the policy to translate 'the N-th cube named in the goal' into a color, then into a field name; the fold stores the positions already in goal order so picks_done indexes them directly.

field red_cube_pos, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  DELETE, folded into target_cube_positions, same reason as blue_cube_pos.

field target_cube_positions, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  NEW (replaces blue_cube_pos, green_cube_pos, red_cube_pos). An ordered list of the [y, x] positions, at the first decision step while the three cubes are still loose and no container is on the table, of exactly the cubes the goal instruction names, in the order the goal names them. Cubes the goal does not name are not recorded. Written at the first decision step and held unchanged for the rest of the episode, even when a container later comes down over a cube or a lifted container briefly re-exposes one (that re-exposed cube wobbles a pixel or two and must not overwrite the value). e.g. for a goal naming the blue cube then the red cube: [[78, 157], [106, 105]]; for a goal naming only the red cube: [[73, 93]]

field green_cube_pos, POLICY PROMPT
  DELETE; replaced by target_cube_positions.

field blue_cube_pos, POLICY PROMPT
  DELETE; replaced by target_cube_positions.

field red_cube_pos, POLICY PROMPT
  DELETE; replaced by target_cube_positions.

field target_cube_positions, POLICY PROMPT
  NEW. If the scene at this decision step shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere (the scene before the button is pressed), read the goal instruction, list the cubes it names in the order it names them, and write the [y, x] of each of those cubes as an ordered list in that same order; leave out any cube the goal does not name. Otherwise copy the carried-in list unchanged, never editing it from a cube briefly exposed under a lifted container. e.g. goal naming blue then red: [[78, 157], [106, 105]]; goal naming only red: [[73, 93]]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Rule 1 stays as it is except that the memory it writes at the first step is target_cube_positions (one entry per goal-named cube, in goal order) instead of three per-color fields. Rule 2 changes its target lookup: when the last frame shows containers on the table and nothing held, choose B and point at the center of the container nearest to the entry of target_cube_positions at index picks_done (the first entry when picks_done is 0, the second when picks_done is 1), written as [y, x]; containers covering no listed position are ignored. Rule 3 is unchanged. The 'all cubes already picked' clause reads: if picks_done equals the length of target_cube_positions, choose C if holding, otherwise B at the container nearest the last entry of the list. The unforeseen-situation clause refers to the next entry of target_cube_positions in the same way. All mentions of blue_cube_pos, green_cube_pos and red_cube_pos are removed.

refused
  No step failed in this minibatch, so nothing from the policy was reported; the only item acted on is the carried-and-never-read field. I did not simply drop green_cube_pos outright and keep blue and red as separate fields, because that would silently break an episode whose goal names the green cube; folding all three into one goal-ordered list keeps every cube that can ever be a target while carrying nothing that is never read.
